To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the resilience of traditional healthcare systems and of communities are interrelated, and the resilience of the systems is influenced by changes in the social-ecological context.

(1) the resilience of THC is affected by the resilience of the communities and (2) the resilience of both systems is influenced by the social, economic, political, cultural, and environmental context.
(i) THS are resilient and adaptable, and (ii) the resilience of THs is influenced by the resilience of the communities and vice versa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the resilience and adaptability of THS in communities in Brazil, which is a topic that has been overlooked by the scientific literature.
the resilience and sustainability of the social-ecological system in which the THS are embedded.
the resilience of THC in the face of changes in the social-ecological systems, and with the resilience of communities in the face of social changes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resilience of the social-ecological systems of the communities studied is related to the resilience of their traditional healthcare systems.
resilience is not a property of a system but an emergent property of a system, and it is a process that is continuously being constructed and reconstructed.

the THS of the communities analyzed have been resilient to different drivers and pressures, but they are still threatened by new drivers and pressures, such as the urbanization processes and the restriction of access and uses of native plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
resilience and adaptability of the THS in Brazil are related to the resilience of the communities, and the latter are influenced by the former.
the resilience of the communities influences the THS and the resilience of the systems influences the resilience of the social-ecological system.

the resilience of the traditional health systems and of the communities is closely interwoven, and the social-ecological perspective can be a useful tool to understand and improve the health of the populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resilience is not only the ability to bounce back to previous conditions, but also the capacity to adapt and change, which is a dynamic process.
the resilience of the traditional healthcare systems of communities in Brazil is related to the resilience of the social-ecological systems where the communities are embedded.

the resilience of communities and of their healthcare systems influence each other, and both can be improved by the recognition of traditional knowledge and practices, the development of partnerships, and the promotion of social capital.
